- **MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank)** measures how high the first relevant result appears. A score of 1 means the first result is relevant; lower values mean the first relevant result tends to appear farther down the list.
- **nDCG (normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain)** measures the quality and ordering of multiple relevant results, giving more credit when highly relevant items appear near the top. It is typically normalized from 0 to 1, where higher is better.

AsterFind used both metrics to evaluate ranking quality, alongside Recall and chronological holdouts, rather than treating plausible-looking recommendations as proof of success. [source:asterfind]
